newsitem.title: UK: UK's Princess Diana to visit Jamaica.
newsitem.headline: UK's Princess Diana to visit Jamaica.

text.p: Britain's Princess Diana will visit Jamaica in October on a medical fund-raising mission, a children's charity said on Friday.
The Chain of Hope said Diana, who sees herself as a beacon for the sick and needy since her divorce from Prince Charles, said the princess would visit the Caribbean on October 24.
She will speak at a banquet in the Jamaican capital of Kingston to raise funds for vital medical equipment needed by local children, the charity said.

Following the collapse of her marriage to Britain's king-in-waiting, Diana said she wanted to be an ambassador for Britain and "Queen of Hearts" reaching out to the world's poor, sick and dispossessed.

She is currently auctioning off a sumptuous wardrobe of old ball gowns to raise money for AIDS and cancer charities, and made headlines with a high-profile trip to Angola highlighting the dangers of landmines.
A spokeswoman for Diana, whose sons are second and third in line for the throne, said no details were yet available about the Jamaica trip.
But she said Diana would attend a fund-raising lunch in London in September to raise money for a Kingston hospital.
The Chain of Hope is a non-profit organisation dedicated to helping children with potentially correctable diseases. It sends medical teams abroad to treat children and train local doctors.
Last year, its patron Sir Magdi Yacoub, a renowned surgeon whose work Diana has followed closely, visited Jamaica to operate on 15 children suffering from life-threatening heart disease.
Diana stirred controversy when she was filmed in full make-up and a surgical mask watching Yacoub perform heart surgery on a young African boy.
